📰 General

DOJ Launches Civil Rights Probe Following Minneapolis Man’s Death at Border •

The Department of Justice has initiated a federal civil rights investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Border Patrol officers fatally shot Pretti on Saturday after a traffic stop. The investigation will examine whether civil rights were violated during the encounter. The DOJ’s probe will focus on the actions of the officers involved and the events leading up to Pretti’s death. Details regarding the initial stop and subsequent shooting are currently under investigation.

🌍 World

New Dutch Government Unveils Ambitious Plan Focused on Climate, Economy, and Social Issues •

The Netherlands’ recently formed minority government released a comprehensive 67-page coalition agreement outlining its key priorities. The plan centers on transitioning to a green economy, aiming to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 and investing heavily in renewable energy. A core element involves significant investment in social programs, including measures to combat poverty and inequality. The government also intends to reform the country’s labor market and address housing shortages, reflecting a commitment to broad societal improvements.

🦅 US

Artemis 2 Mission Advances: SLS Rocket Fueling Test Scheduled for February •

NASA is preparing for a crucial test of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket ahead of the Artemis II mission. The upcoming fueling test, slated for February 2nd, will be conducted at Kennedy Space Center. This test is a critical step in verifying the rocket’s capabilities for the first crewed lunar flight since 1972. NASA will be closely monitoring the event via live video streams from the launch site.

💰 Business

Trump Nominates Former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh for Federal Reserve Chair •

President Donald Trump announced his intention to nominate Kevin M. Warsh as the next chair of the Federal Reserve. Warsh, a former governor under Janet Yellen, was a vocal critic of the Fed’s monetary policy during his tenure. The nomination represents a significant shift, as Warsh advocates for greater transparency and accountability within the central bank. This selection is expected to generate considerable debate among policymakers and economists regarding the Fed’s future direction.

💻 Technology

iPhone 18 Pro Rumored to Feature Camera Advantages Over Foldable Model •

Apple is expected to release three new flagship iPhones this fall: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Fold. Recent reports suggest the standard iPhone Pro models will boast enhanced camera capabilities compared to the foldable device. Specifically, the Pro line is rumored to incorporate improvements in optical zoom and low-light performance. These advancements are intended to differentiate the Pro iPhones from Apple’s foldable offerings. Details regarding the exact specifications remain unconfirmed pending official announcements.

🎭 Entertainment

Catherine O’Hara, ‘Schitt’s Creek’ Star, Dies at 71 After Brief Illness •

Catherine O’Hara, known for her roles in “Home Alone,” “Schitt’s Creek,” and “Best in Show,” passed away on Friday at her Los Angeles home. Her manager confirmed she was 71 years old and had been suffering from a brief illness. O’Hara’s career spanned decades, marked by comedic performances and memorable characters. She is survived by her husband and children.

🏅 Sports

Vikings Terminate GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Following Below-Expectation Season •

The Minnesota Vikings have dismissed general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah following a 9-8 regular season campaign. The decision comes after the team failed to meet initial expectations for the 2023 season. Vice President of Football Operations Rob Brzezinski will assume interim leadership of the team’s football operations. The Vikings’ board of directors made the call after evaluating the team’s performance and strategic direction. This marks the end of Adofo-Mensah’s tenure with the franchise.

🔬 Science

Scientists Drill Into Thwaites Glacier to Unlock Secrets of Antarctic Melt •

Researchers have initiated drilling operations through the Thwaites Glacier in West Antarctica to investigate the glacier’s stability and rate of melting. The project, a collaboration between British and South Korean scientists, aims to collect ice core samples from deep within the glacier. These samples will be analyzed to understand the processes driving the glacier’s rapid retreat and its potential impact on global sea levels. The team is particularly focused on examining the layers of ice to determine how much water is trapped within the glacier and how that water is contributing to its movement.

🩺 Health

Wegovy, Mounjaro Linked to Rare Pancreatitis and Patient Deaths in UK •

The UK’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has issued a warning regarding a potential link between the obesity drugs Wegovy and Mounjaro and cases of severe pancreatitis. Multiple patients have reportedly died due to this inflammation of the pancreas, although the occurrences remain statistically rare. The MHRA is investigating the connection and advising healthcare professionals to be vigilant for symptoms. The agency is also urging patients to seek immediate medical attention if experiencing unexplained abdominal pain.
